questions.question: Which urban legend involves a phantom attacker who is said to assault victims with gas?
questions.explanation_correct: The Mad Gasser is a classic American urban legend about an unseen assailant allegedly releasing gas on victims. The story circulated in reports of panic and strange nighttime incidents.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Grey Lady and Teke Teke are ghostly figures, while Polybius is a game legend. None of those are the gas-based phantom attacker.

questions.question: Which roadside legend is commonly described as a spectral canine appearing near travelers?
questions.explanation_correct: The Black dog is a recurring folklore and urban legend figure seen along roads or lonely places. It is often treated as an omen or supernatural warning.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Men in Black are mysterious agents, Dover Demon is a cryptid, and La Llorona is a grieving woman spirit. None of those are the canine roadside apparition.

questions.question: Which forest is widely associated with Japanese folklore and supernatural reputation?
questions.explanation_correct: Aokigahara is a forest in Japan that has become strongly associated with folklore and ghost stories. Its reputation has made it a frequent subject of urban legend discussions.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Dover Demon is a cryptid, Polybius is an arcade legend, and Dybbuk box is a haunted object. None of those are the forest location tied to Japanese supernatural lore.

questions.question: Which creature is described in cryptid lore as a small, humanoid figure reported in Massachusetts?
questions.explanation_correct: The Dover Demon is a well-known cryptid reported in Dover, Massachusetts, with a humanoid appearance. It is one of the more famous regional creature legends.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Grey Lady is a ghostly woman, Mad Gasser is a phantom attacker, and Black dog is a roadside apparition. None of those are the small humanoid cryptid from Massachusetts.

questions.question: Which prisoner was nicknamed the “Birdman of Alcatraz”?
questions.explanation_correct: Robert Stroud was a real prisoner known as the Birdman of Alcatraz, though he kept and studied birds earlier at Leavenworth.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names belong to different historical figures; Stroud was the prisoner known by that nickname.

questions.question: What is the name of the phantom big cat associated with Cornwall?
questions.explanation_correct: The Beast of Bodmin is the famous alleged big cat linked to Bodmin Moor in Cornwall. It is one of Britain’s best-known phantom feline legends.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices are different British folklore creatures or invented-style names, not the Bodmin big cat legend.

questions.question: Which red-cloaked Japanese restroom spirit asks a victim to choose between red and blue paper?
questions.explanation_correct: Aka Manto, meaning “Red Cape” or “Red Cloak,” appears in Japanese bathroom-ghost stories involving a choice of paper.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Hanako-san is also a school-bathroom ghost, but Aka Manto is the red-cloaked figure in this story.

questions.question: Which forest on the edge of London is associated with local ghost stories?
questions.explanation_correct: Epping Forest, on the edge of London and in Essex, has long been associated with local ghost stories.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other forests are in Germany, Romania and Japan.

questions.question: What is the title of the creepypasta about a supposedly disturbing lost episode featuring a SpongeBob SquarePants character?
questions.explanation_correct: “Squidward’s Suicide” is a fictional lost-episode creepypasta involving the SpongeBob character Squidward.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other titles refer to different stories or horror tropes.

questions.question: What is the name of the classic urban legend about giant reptiles living in the sewers of New York City?
questions.explanation_correct: Sewer alligators are a classic pop-culture trope based on the idea that flushed pets grew into massive monsters in the city tunnels.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are made-up names that do not correspond to the well-known urban myth.

questions.question: What Spanish term is often used for a small goblin-like being in many Latin American folklore traditions?
questions.explanation_correct: A duende is a small supernatural being in Spanish-language folklore; its appearance and behavior vary across regions.
questions.explanation_incorrect: La Llorona, the chupacabra and el Cadejo are different figures in folklore.

questions.question: Which urban legend from Eastern Europe tells of a black luxury car that drives around at night abducting people?
questions.explanation_correct: The Black Volga is a mysterious car said to stalk cities in the Soviet era, allegedly used by officials or sinister forces to kidnap victims.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are fictional generic ghost-vehicle names and do not represent a specific urban legend.

questions.question: Near which Oregon city did officials use explosives on a stranded whale carcass in 1970, an incident later shared widely online?
questions.explanation_correct: The exploding-whale incident happened near Florence, Oregon, in 1970 and was filmed by a television news crew.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The filmed incident occurred near Florence, not the other Oregon cities.

questions.question: What is the Icelandic name for the giant Yule Cat of Christmas folklore?
questions.explanation_correct: Jólakötturinn is the Icelandic name for the Yule Cat, a giant cat in Christmas folklore.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names refer to different figures in European folklore.
